items.claim: The אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי marker (how much more / how much less) binds both half-verses into one a-fortiori argument, and neither neighbor shares a root with 17:7.
items.evidence: 17:7 reads lo naavah lenaval sefat yeter, אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי lenadiv sefat shaqer -- the אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי conjunction structurally subordinates clause two to clause one as a single escalating claim, not two juxtaposed sayings. 17:6 (ateret zeqenim beney vanim...) and 17:8 (even chen hashochad...) share no lexical root with 17:7; the boundary is clean on both sides.

items.claim: 17:13 carries the book K/Q note at its verb (תמיש תָמ֥וּשׁ), matching the pmarks inventory exactly, and the retribution maxim shares no root with 17:12 or 17:14.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq lists Prov.17.13: 1 -- the sole K/Q note for this verse, confirming the row single-witness disclosure at the correct verb (תמיש תָמ֥וּשׁ). 17:12 (pagosh dov shakkul...) and 17:14 (poter mayim reshit madon...) share no lexical root with 17:13 meshiv/raah/tovah/tamush/beyt set.

items.claim: 17:20 pairs עִקֶּשׁ לֵ֭ב and וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ as two closely matched crooked subject-types closed within the verse; no root recurs in 17:19 or 17:21.
items.evidence: 17:20 pairs a crooked-heart subject (עִקֶּשׁ לֵ֭ב) failing to find good with a perverted-tongue subject (וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ) falling into evil -- synthetic, not antithetic (no vav-adversative), matching the row device_notes. 17:19 (ohev pesha...) and 17:21 (yoled kesil...) share no root with 17:20.

items.claim: The shared noun kesil (17:24 כְ֝סִ֗יל / 17:25 כְּסִ֑יל) is disclosed and correctly defeated as glue: 17:24 fool is the wandering-eyed subject of its own clause, 17:25 fool is a construct modifier inside a different clause -- a repeated word, not a repeated construction.
items.evidence: 17:24 et peney mevin chokhmah veeyney כְ֝סִ֗יל biqtseh arets closes on the fool own roving eyes; 17:25 opens kaas leaviv ben כְּסִ֑יל with the fool as the grieved-over son. No construct chain, word order, or syntactic slot is shared between the two kesil occurrences beyond the bare lexeme.

items.claim: The rationale quotes WEB own clause wording in straight quotes with no inline web: ref in the same field, where the book-wide convention requires curly quotes plus an in-field web: ref for verbatim WEB text.
items.evidence: WEB Prov.17.25 reads (web:Prov.17.25): “A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.” -- the row straight-quoted spans "to his father" and "her who bore him" are exact substrings of that WEB clause, not independent glosses of the Hebrew (leaviv / leyoladto), so they fall under the WEB-quotation convention rather than the straight-quote gloss convention; the rationale field itself carries no web: token to satisfy the in-field pairing rule.

items.claim: 18:1 יִתְגַּלָּֽע (root gimel-lamed-ayin, burst forth) and 18:2 בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת (root gimel-lamed-he, reveal) are visually similar but consonantally distinct roots -- not a shared catchword -- and 17:28 shares no root with 18:1 either, so the single-verse call is correctly held despite the two verses shared self-isolation theme.
items.evidence: 18:1 closes bekhol tushiyah יִתְגַּלָּֽע (ayin-final root); 18:2 closes ki im בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת libo (he-final root). The final radical differs (ayin vs he), so despite the near-homograph shape there is no shared lexical root to cite as cross-seam cohesion. 17:28 (gam evil machrish...) shares no root with 18:1.

items.claim: 18:6 opens שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל and closes וּ֝פִ֗יו; 18:7 opens פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל and closes וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו -- an exact chiastic reversal (lips...mouth // mouth...lips) on the same construct-chain slot and the same head noun kesil, meeting the owner construction-run bar for proverb_cluster; neighbors 18:5 and 18:8 share no root, so both cluster boundaries hold.
items.evidence: 18:5 (seet peney rasha...) and 18:8 (divrey nirgan...) carry no peh/safah/kesil token, confirming the cluster start and end seams are clean and the construction does not straddle undisclosed.

items.claim: 18:9 equivalence clause (אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא levaal mashchit, brother he is to a master of destruction) is self-contained; no root recurs in 18:8 or 18:10.
items.evidence: 18:8 (divrey nirgan kemitlahamim...) and 18:10 (migdal oz shem YHWH...) share no lexical root with 18:9 gam/mitrapeh/melakhto/ach/baal/mashchit set.
